clue.text: Superficial type replaces wife during lottery

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a letter is swapped out and the type word put in its place
during places the swap inside the lottery word, telling us where the exchange happens

blocks.note: a sweep, short for sweepstake, is a lottery
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a kind is a type or sort

explanation.surface: Someone shallow takes the wife's place in a raffle draw.
explanation.walkthrough: KIND goes where the W of SWEEP was, giving SKIN-DEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes no further than the outer layer is shallow, lacking any real depth beneath.

clue.text: Drink starts to kick in rapidly

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A drink whose effect is felt almost at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur, a mixed alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Idea lacking information? Either way it's unacceptable

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so a letter must be taken away from the idea word
reading the same either way, forwards or backwards, describes a word that reverses into itself

blocks.note: a notion is an idea
I is the abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: An idea with no facts behind it is simply not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTION without its I leaves NOTON, which reads the same backwards: NOT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not on' is a British idiom meaning something is not allowed or not acceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Coming to this planet and unable to leave it

blocks.note: first meaning: heading towards our world, as a returning spacecraft is
second meaning: tied to the ground, unable to fly or escape

explanation.surface: A spacecraft returning home that then finds itself stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' means both 'headed for' and 'tied down', so the one word covers both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound for our world means travelling towards it; bound to the ground means trapped there, never able to fly.

clue.text: Function without latitude to some extent

indicators.note: in the old sense, without means outside, so the function word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: a party is a social function
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A party held without some freedom is only partly enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside': L sits inside PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly is an adverb meaning in part, not completely, which is the same as to a certain degree.

clue.text: Congested excavation channel turned over

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so the joined words are read backwards

blocks.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
a rut is a groove or channel in the ground

explanation.surface: A blocked channel on a dig site has been overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgid describes something swollen and distended, as tissue congested with fluid becomes.

clue.text: Do spies keep them behind bars for drinking?

definitions.note: describes the things rather than naming them

blocks.note: first meaning: spies 'keep ... on' people they watch
second meaning: running accounts held by bar staff for customers

explanation.surface: A question whether spies hold something in prison for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests prison, but it means behind a pub counter, where drinkers' running bills are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep tabs on someone is to watch them closely; a bar tab is a customer's running bill for drinks.

clue.text: Reason for relationship having spirit returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the spirit word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a ratio is the relationship between two quantities
elan is spirit or verve

explanation.surface: Looking for why a relationship regained its spark.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the spirit word is turned round; the relationship word stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying set of reasons or logical basis behind a course of action.

clue.text: Surprisingly, Nato win case to get scientist

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, hinting that the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unexpected legal victory for the military alliance brings in an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

clue.text: Journalist perhaps gets server to pull article for recipe

indicators.note: to pull something is to withdraw it, and with 'for' it signals one letter swapped out for another

blocks.note: a waiter serves at table
A is the indefinite article
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A food columnist has a waiter remove an item from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in WAITER is replaced by R, giving WRITER.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist is one example of someone who produces written work professionally, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Defence is behind in concrete case

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it, with the concrete word acting as the case around it

blocks.note: concrete means real or actual; 'case' marks it as the outer shell
a butt is a person's behind

explanation.surface: A lawyer's defence relies on someone being encased in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' tells you the concrete word is the outer shell; 'behind' is the rear end, not 'late'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counter-argument offered to refute a charge or claim, a form of answering back.

clue.text: Intend storing heroin in craft for now

indicators.note: storing something means keeping it inside, so the craft word holds the drug letter

blocks.note: to mean is to intend
craft in the sense of cunning or a crafty trick
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A smuggler plans to keep drugs hidden in a boat for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat, but it means cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile is an adverb meaning in the intervening period, until something else happens, like 'for the present'.

clue.text: Blade cast in fragments can be a flexible thing

indicators.note: smashed into fragments, the letters are broken up and must be reassembled differently

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged, the little word 'in' included

explanation.surface: A cast blade that shatters turns out to have been bendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as part of 'in fragments', but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber band stretches and springs back, so it is a typical example of something pliable and stretchy.

clue.text: It's light and carried for love

blocks.note: first meaning: a portable lamp
second meaning: in the idiom of carrying one for someone you secretly love

explanation.surface: Describing something that is not heavy and is borne for affection.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry a torch for someone is to love them without its being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a handheld lamp in British English, and the idiom about unrequited affection uses the same word.

clue.text: Checkout times suit individual circumstances

definitions.note: the answer is an adverbial phrase, 'treating individual circumstances separately'

blocks.note: to case a place is to check it out before a robbery
'by' means times, as in three by four
a suit is a law case

explanation.surface: Supermarket tills that adapt to each shopper's situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checkout' looks like a supermarket till but is the verb 'check out', as a burglar does.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing with matters case by case means handling each one separately on its own particular merits.

clue.text: Start filming battle

blocks.note: first meaning: the director's call to begin a take
second meaning: combat, as in troops seeing it

explanation.surface: An order to begin shooting a war film.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director shouts the word to begin a take; soldiers 'in' it are engaged in military combat.

clue.text: Fancy art deco from middle area of Paris

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, so only those of the preceding word are kept
fancy as a verb means to dress up or elaborate, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Ornate 1920s design taken from the heart of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link but supplies its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trocadéro is a district of Paris facing the Eiffel Tower across the Seine, famous for its Art Deco palace.

clue.text: Nice lady using first name to interrupt me

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something, so the name goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
Adam was the first man, so his is the first name

explanation.surface: A pleasant woman keeps using someone's first name to cut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not 'pleasant'; at the start of the clue its capital letter gives nothing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, so a lady in the French city would be addressed this way.

clue.text: Brace before lift-off? To a degree, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a brace is a pair, and the countdown says the pair followed by the single just before launch
second meaning: an upper second, the usual British university degree grade

explanation.surface: Preparing oneself before take-off, to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' looks like 'somewhat', but 'To' is a link. A British honours degree is graded first, two-one, two-two or third.
explanation.definitionFit: The final counts before launch are 'two, one'; a 2:1 is an upper-second-class British university honours grade.

clue.text: What's at stake restrains whistleblower; that's very sad

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold something in, so the stake word holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: a bet is the sum staked
a referee blows the whistle in a match

explanation.surface: Money on the line silences a leaker of secrets, which is a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests a leaker, but it is the official who blows a whistle in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived of something loved, especially through bereavement, and so desolate or deeply sorrowful.

clue.text: Locate stand-in turning up in row

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom to the top, so the joined words run backwards

blocks.note: to put something is to locate or place it
a sub is a substitute

explanation.surface: Finding a replacement causes trouble when arguments break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is the argument sense, rhyming with 'cow', not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is a British informal word for a noisy quarrel or fight between people.

clue.text: Small crowd get lost

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to crowd into a space is to cram

explanation.surface: A modest gathering of people goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a rude command telling someone to leave at once, just like the dismissive order 'go away'.

clue.text: Obliged to make tax limited

blocks.note: a duty is a tax on goods
bound means restricted or limited

explanation.surface: Forced to set a ceiling on a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone duty-bound is morally or legally required to act, compelled by a sense of responsibility.

clue.text: Prepare popular backing section for classical music

indicators.note: a section is just a part, so the letters lie inside the run of words given
going backwards means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Getting a well-loved supporting part ready for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters AREPO sit across 'prepARE POpular'; read backwards they give OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a dramatic art form set to orchestral music, part of the Western art-music tradition.

clue.text: Lost without commercial break

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the commercial letters must be taken away

blocks.note: adrift means lost, drifting without direction
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Missing out on an advertising pause on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial break' looks like one phrase; split it, and 'break' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a crack or split in something, or a breach in a friendship.

clue.text: In truth, life is complicated — this makes it look better

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so these letters are mixed into a new order
placing one thing in another means setting it inside, so the jumbled letters go within the truth word

blocks.note: a fact is a truth
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A philosophical sigh that life is hard, and something to cheer it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In truth' reads as 'honestly' but marks the container, and only 'life' is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic surgical procedure tightens the skin of the face to make the patient appear younger.

clue.text: Bureau sounding out new college after some time

indicators.note: sounding something out means saying it aloud, so the letters are read as spoken sounds

blocks.note: some time is an age, then N for new and C for college; said aloud as 'age-en-see'

explanation.surface: An office announcing a new college opening after a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the time first. Spoken as letters, AGE, N and C run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an organisation or office providing a particular service, such as a government department.

clue.text: Hint — what you're reading is missing line

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so a letter is removed from the thing being read

blocks.note: the solver is reading a crossword clue
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A tip that the text in front of you has dropped a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt, such as an actor's cue to speak, which suggests what to do.

clue.text: Expert made errors with central pieces

indicators.note: the central pieces of each word are its middle letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters
the two middle letters
the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A specialist made blunders in the key parts of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link but supplies letters too.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever with one's hands or mind, so as an adjective it matches being highly skilled.

clue.text: Pet adder gone astray — it happened earlier

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer's sense: came before

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered off course, so the letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet snake has escaped, and the owner says it occurred before.
explanation.walkthrough: With a snake about, 'predator' comes to mind, but the time sense wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate something is to come before it in time, existing or occurring at an earlier date.
